connected_surface.create_commit: Available. The connector accepts an explicit tree SHA plus a required parent SHA and optional additional parents.
connected_surface.update_ref: Available. The connector accepts branch_name, target SHA, and force=false by default; it exposes no expected-old/current-SHA compare-and-swap parameter.
connected_surface.reason_no_live_ref_mutation: Role-local write authority is path-scoped to cross_field state/receipts and primary/direct-main authority is forbidden. The bounded test therefore used connector schema plus official public GitHub Git-object/ref semantics rather than mutating a repository ref.

official_public_sources.fact: Update-a-reference takes target sha plus force; force omitted/false requires a fast-forward update rather than overwriting work. No expected-old SHA is part of the request body.
Create-a-commit takes a tree and an ordered parents array, so an explicit parent can anchor a proposed child commit.

case_analysis.case: current ref still equals expected parent P
case_analysis.outcome: A child C with parent P is a fast-forward; non-force update to C can succeed.

case_analysis.case: concurrent ordinary forward movement moved ref from P to descendant Q
case_analysis.outcome: C(parent=P) and Q diverge after P, so moving Q to C is non-fast-forward and is rejected.

case_analysis.case: ordinary revert implemented as a new commit after Q
case_analysis.outcome: The ref remains a descendant of P; moving it to sibling C is non-fast-forward and is rejected.

case_analysis.case: force-ref rewind restores ref to P (or an ancestor of P)
case_analysis.outcome: Moving the rewound ref to C becomes a fast-forward and can succeed even though intervening history existed. The guard therefore cannot distinguish ABA caused by ref rewind.

evidence.semantic_conclusion: Explicit-parent commit plus force=false ref update is an ancestry/fast-forward stale-write guard, not true expected-old CAS. It protects against concurrent forward movement and ordinary revert commits but is defeated by a force-ref rewind that restores an ancestor. Because the only remembered anchor would still have to live on rewindable repository state, this surface does not close r201's non-rewindable-anchor gap by itself.
